what: The page says go vet flags comparing a value with itself (`x == x`). It doesn't: I ran Go 1.27.3's vet in scratch and it reported nothing for `x == x`. It does flag `x != 1 || x != 2` (suspect or) and `x > 5 && x > 5` (redundant and).
evidence: Page: "The `go vet` and editor helpers flag a few of this chapter's slips that still compile, such as comparing a value with itself (`x == x`) or a condition that is always true or always false." Scratch run of go vet (go1.27.3): "main.go:6:5: suspect or: x != 1 || x != 2", "main.go:7:5: redundant and: x > 5 && x > 5", and no report for line 5 `fmt.Println(x == x)`.
fix: Replace the example: "such as `x != 1 || x != 2`, which is always true (vet calls it a 'suspect or'), or the same question twice, `x > 5 && x > 5`." Better still, capture a vet run of it.

what: The caption says `for i := range 3 {` "Means exactly" the three-part loop. It doesn't quite. The range form works out n once and gives a new value to i every lap, so assigning to i inside the body doesn't change the number of laps; in the three-part form it does. The page's own notebook says n "is worked out once".
evidence: Caption: "Means exactly `for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {`, with less to type...". Go spec, For statements with range clause (integer range): the iteration values are 0 to n-1, and n is evaluated once.
fix: Change "Means exactly" to "Does the same job as".
